data.title: Anthropic IPO Shares May Have Favored Heavy Claude Users, Investors Suspect
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, some investors suspect Anthropic favored heavy users of its Claude model in allocating IPO shares, though the company also distributed large allocations to major institutions including Citadel. More than half of the shares reportedly went to existing investors, including Altimeter Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures. About 60% of institutions that ordered shares received none, while BlackRock reportedly sought about $10 billion worth and received roughly half that amount.

Anthropic shares rose more than 30% above the offering price when trading began Thursday, then closed up 17%. On Friday, they fell as much as 15%, briefly trading just 5 cents above the offer price, before closing down 8.5% at $88.91, still 7% above the offering price. The company’s market value fell by about $109 billion. Nvidia, Meta and Oracle also declined, and the Nasdaq market lost a combined $4 trillion in value. Anthropic’s IPO and concurrent placement raised more than $100 billion; the IPO allocation was valued at $81 billion.

The allocation drew criticism from investors who said they received fewer shares than requested or none at all. One hedge fund manager also questioned the underwriters’ decision on the opening time and price. Some current and former employees were permitted to sell about 300 million shares immediately, worth roughly $26 billion at the offering price, rather than face the usual lockup. Anthropic said Friday morning that the underwriters had fully exercised the IPO’s 15% greenshoe option. About 300 million more shares are due to become tradable on December 15.

The selloff also weighed on plans by rival OpenAI, which plans to go public next year and is pursuing a large funding round at a post-money valuation of $1.25 trillion. Meanwhile, some San Francisco AI workers focused on a claim by an Anthropic mathematician that Claude had solved a 167-year-old Millennium Prize problem.

data.title: Predict.fun Adds Prediction Event on Amazon’s Year-End 2026 Market Cap
data.description:
Predict.fun has added a prediction event on Amazon’s market capitalization at the end of 2026. According to Odaily, settlement will be based on Amazon’s public market capitalization at the close of regular trading on the final trading day of 2026, calculated by multiplying the official closing price of its shares on the primary exchange by the total shares outstanding at that time.

The calculation may include all classes of outstanding shares, using applicable conversion ratios; shares without conversion rights will be counted as disclosed unless official company documents specify otherwise. The share count will be determined from company filings or disclosures. If the market capitalization falls exactly on a boundary between two ranges, it will be assigned to the higher range.

If Amazon acquires or merges with another entity and remains the parent company, the same calculation will apply. If Amazon is acquired, ceases to be the surviving parent after a merger, or is no longer an independent entity before the period ends, settlement will use the public market capitalization reached before the transaction is completed and will exclude transaction, acquisition or merger consideration. Settlement will rely on official exchange data and publicly disclosed share counts.

data.title: Yi Lihua: Market Decline Reflects Global Financial Risks and Liquidity Crisis, Not Crypto Data
data.description:
Yi Lihua (JackYi) said on X that he had said a week earlier he was no longer considering buying the dip. According to Odaily, he said the current market trend was unrelated to Bitcoin data and was instead tied to global financial risks and a liquidity crisis. He said he had never seen all assets fall sharply together over a short period and that the market bottom could not be predicted before a correction in U.S. stocks stabilized.

Yi said spot holders could withstand a market decline if they had income from outside the market. Otherwise, he advised preparing for extreme market conditions, avoiding leverage and maintaining cash reserves.

data.title: Ken Griffin’s $3 Billion Gift Goes to Carnegie Mellon After Talks With Oxford, Cambridge and MIT
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Citadel CEO Ken Griffin will give Carnegie Mellon University $3 billion: $2 billion to establish a campus in Miami and $1 billion for its main campus in Pittsburgh. Carnegie Mellon called it the largest single personal donation in higher education history. Griffin is not an alumnus; he has donated at least $500 million to Harvard, his alma mater.

Griffin had also discussed a Miami campus with Oxford University, the University of Cambridge and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Talks with MIT, which spanned several years, did not produce an agreement. Oxford discussions in 2024 drew interest from some officials but opposition from others, while talks with Cambridge remained preliminary. Vanderbilt University also met with Griffin but chose West Palm Beach for its Florida campus.

The planned Carnegie Mellon campus will cover 35 acres in Miami’s Wynwood neighborhood. About $1.1 billion of the donation is earmarked for land acquisition and approximately $900 million for construction. Plans call for more than 3,500 undergraduate and graduate students, nearly 300 faculty members and over 600 staff. Construction is scheduled to begin in 2027, with the first students expected in 2028.

Griffin moved the headquarters of his hedge fund, Citadel, and market maker Citadel Securities from Chicago to Miami in 2022. Carnegie Mellon said it will lead campus construction, set academic standards and hire faculty. Griffin joined the university’s board as part of the agreement.

data.title: Hong Kong Bill Would Exclude Tokenized Deposits From Virtual Asset Definition
data.description:
Hong Kong’s government has gazetted the Virtual Asset Service Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026, which would explicitly exclude tokenized deposits from the definition of virtual assets.

According to Odaily, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has described tokenized deposits issued by commercial banks as private money on the currency side of its digital currency framework, rather than assets. Tokenized deposits are also at the core of sandbox trials under Ensemble, Hong Kong’s project to develop a tokenized ecosystem.

The exclusion is expected to give banks and other market participants clearer legal and regulatory certainty, and avoid traditional deposits being brought under a separate virtual-asset regulatory framework solely because they use blockchain or tokenization. The approach reflects the principle of “same business, same risk, same regulation”: changing a product’s technological form should not alter its legal status. It would also provide clearer, more predictable rules for banks to advance tokenized deposits and on-chain payment and settlement innovation.

data.title: Robert Kiyosaki Says He Will Wait for Bitcoin to Bottom Again Before Buying
data.description: Robert Kiyosaki, author of “Rich Dad Poor Dad,” said he plans to wait for Bitcoin to reach another bottom before buying. According to Foresight News, Kiyosaki advised investors not to “catch a falling knife” and to wait until a market decline ends before entering. He said he began buying Bitcoin at $20,000 per coin after the previous market crash and will wait for another bottom this time. Kiyosaki added that profits are made when buying, not when selling.

data.title: Hong Kong Bill Proposes HK$100,000 Fine for Unauthorized Crypto Titles, Two-Year Jail Term for Fake License Claims
data.description:
Hong Kong’s proposed virtual asset legislation would penalize unauthorized use of regulated service-provider titles and false claims of being a license applicant. According to Foresight News, citing Caixin, the 2026 Virtual Asset Service Legislation (Amendment) Bill introduces two offenses to address misleading promotions in the sector.

Anyone who is not licensed or registered but uses titles associated with virtual asset service providers regulated by the Securities and Futures Commission, such as “crypto trader,” “cryptocurrency adviser” or “virtual asset custodian,” could face a HK$100,000 fine upon conviction. Continuing violations would carry an additional HK$2,000 fine for each day they persist.

A person falsely claiming to be a license applicant could, upon conviction on indictment, face a HK$400,000 fine and up to two years in prison. Each day of a continuing offense could bring an additional HK$10,000 fine.

data.title: DWF Labs Says Bitcoin Tracks Nasdaq Rather Than Acting as Digital Gold
data.description: DWF Labs said Bitcoin is not digital gold and tends to track the Nasdaq. According to PANews, Bitcoin has shown its strongest correlation with stocks; since spot ETFs launched in 2020, its correlation with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq has remained around 0.39. When the Nasdaq fell by more than 1%, Bitcoin also declined about three-quarters of the time, while gold fell 57% of the time over the same period. Bitcoin’s correlation with gold has generally been weak, but its 90-day correlation rose to 0.59 in September 2026, a 10-year high.
